findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing or unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| IoError::Read { path: path.to_owned(), source: e })

findings.problem: File I/O (fs::read_to_string) is fused inside the packet-loading function alongside parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: shell I/O is mixed with domain parsing, violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation; the pure parsing cannot be unit-tested or reasoned about independently
findings.fix: Split into two functions: load_packets_bytes(path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IoError> for the shell boundary, and parse_packets(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> for the pure calculation layer

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effect inside the mapping closure that should be pure parsing
findings.failure_mode: logging escapes into what should be a pure calculation; breaks deterministic evaluation, complicates testing, and couples data construction to a specific output mechanism
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parser. If metrics/logging are needed, perform them at the shell layer after parse_packets returns, not inside the mapping closure

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing on a split result with no bounds validation
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields triggers an IndexOutOfBounds panic at runtime; no bounds check, no get() guard, no split_once fallback
findings.fix: Replace the split/collect/index pattern with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Malformed)? to extract name and value_str safely, eliminating all index access

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: any parsed value greater than 65535 silently truncates to a wrong u16 value; the cast discards high-order bits without any range check, producing invalid domain state
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) instead of the as cast, and wrap the entire parse+convert chain with map_err to return a typed Overflow error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value fields
findings.failure_mode: malformed numeric input in any packet line causes an unrecoverable panic instead of returning a typed parse error like ParseError::Invalid
findings.fix: Replace .unwrap() with .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and propagate through Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String and pub value: u16 — raw primitives expose the parse boundary with no smart constructor
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct Record with any String for name and any u16 for value, including values that violate domain rules; illegal states are representable because no validation occurs at construction
findings.fix: Define newtypes PacketName(String) with a smart constructor that validates length/alphabet, use enum Status for lifecycle, and make Record fields private with a private constructor that enforces invariants

findings.problem: load_packets returns an unbounded Vec<Record> with no domain cap or try_reserve, and intermediate Vec<String> allocated per line
findings.failure_mode: an adversarial file with millions of lines causes unbounded heap growth and per-line Vec allocation, enabling DoS; no try_reserve, no max_rows cap, no bounded allocation discipline
findings.fix: Validate a domain max_rows cap before iteration; use Vec::new() then values.try_reserve(min(cap, max_rows)).map_err(|_| AllocationError)?; avoid per-line intermediate Vec by iterating over split directly

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for the load_packets function; no workload or performance claim is documented
findings.failure_mode: without baseline measurements, any optimization claim is ungrounded; intermediate Vec<String> per line and unbounded allocation are invisible to unmeasured code
findings.fix: Add a criterion or divan benchmark exercising realistic input sizes; measure allocation count, throughput, and latency before and after any optimization

no second-ring evidence for any performance or correctness claim

residual_risk: Static review only — no commands executed. The source contains 2 unwrap() panic surfaces, 1 hidden I/O (println!) in pure logic, 1 hidden I/O (fs::read_to_string) fused with parsing, 1 lossy u32-to-u16 cast, 1 unchecked indexing on split parts, 1 unbounded allocation with no try_reserve, raw-primitive domain fields without newtypes or smart constructors, and no benchmark/profiler/test evidence. All 6 absolute-law violations (unwrap, hidden I/O, unchecked indexing, lossy cast) are BLOCKERs requiring repair before any delivery gate.
